candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 75 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 76 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 77 the word should in Agency guidance means that something is suggested or recommended, but 78 not required. 79
candidates.context: I. Introduction 65 The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is issuing this guidance to provide labeling 66 recommendations for hernia mesh devices. These labeling recommendations are being issued 67 because suboptimal device selection associated with these devices has resulted in serious adverse 68 events, including deaths. 1 The package labeling recommendations in this guidance, including the 69 example in Appendix A below, are intended to help promote the safe and effective use of hernia 70 mesh. When finalized, this guidance is intended to supplement the labeling recommendations in 71 section XI of “ Guidance for the Preparation of a Premarket Notification Application for a 72 Surgical Mesh,” for hernia mesh devices. 73 II. Background 81 Hernia meshes represent a diverse group of medical devices featuring a wide variety of 82 compositions, form factors, shapes, sizes, materia

candidates.statement: 4 This guidance is not intended to include a complete listing of all labeling requirements under the FD&C Act and FDA regulations that are applicable to hernia mesh. Also, this guidance should be used as a complement to other relevant FDA guidance documents containing additional labeling recommendations.
candidates.context: 3 “Adequate directions for use means directions under which the layman can use a device safely and for the purposes for which it is intended.” 21 CFR 801.5. o Mesh composition (including the specific materials used, and whether those 134 materials are absorbable synthetic, nonabsorbable synthetic, or biologic) 135  Identification of the source of any biologic/animal-derived materials 136 o Identification of barrier material, if present 137 o Identification and description of any added ingredients, such as antimicrobials 138

candidates.statement: FDA believes that the device description and instruction information identified above will help 163 mitigate the safety issues associated with hernia meshes and help manufacturers develop 164 informative package labeling consistent with the labeling requirements under 21 CFR 801.109. 165 Since these recommendations are based on known safety issues, FDA recommends that this 166 information be considered for inclusion as current product labeling is updated, and that labeling 167 included as part of future premarket submissions for hernia meshes incorporate the 168 recommendations. For currently marketed hernia meshes, manufacturers should evaluate their 169 labeling changes as recommended in FDA’s guidance, “ Deciding When to Submit a 510(k) for a 170 Change to an Existing Device .” 171
